subject: POC evaluation path: Shadow vs. offline + grading rubric (next steps)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Romero <alex.romero@novalabs.com>, Novalabs POC <poc@novalabs.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed POC evaluation options

Hi Alex / Novalabs team,

Thanks again for the call today — good context on the customer service use cases and the 3 primary success signals you called out (extraction accuracy, end-to-end latency for live assist, and reductions in manual escalations). As promised, here are the two viable POC evaluation routes we recommend and a suggested quick rubric so we can align on scope quickly: 

1) Live Shadow (recommended for low-latency assist):
- Redwood runs inference in shadow mode against a 7-day live stream of representative traffic.
- Measures: token-level latency percentiles, normalized extraction F1 on curated ground-truths, and operator acceptance rate on triaged tickets.
- Pros: realistic latency and system integration; catches infra and routing edge cases.
- Cons: requires short-term access to a redacted subset of live traffic and an on-call stakeholder for triage.

2) Offline Batch (recommended if data access is constrained):
- Run the same model on historical/exported records (1–2k examples) with structured eval harness.
- Measures: extraction F1, end-to-end simulated latency, and ranking precision at top-k.
- Pros: quick to run, minimal infra access.
- Cons: may miss integration-induced latency/regression modes.

Proposed high-level success criteria (we can formalize these into the attached spreadsheet):
- Extraction F1 >= 0.88 on held-out set
- 95th percentile inference latency < 350ms (shadow) / simulated p95 < 300ms (offline)
- Manual escalation rate reduction >= 25% (relative) during the observation window

Next steps I propose:
- You pick preferred route (shadow or offline) by Thursday 7/22
- We provision temporary shadow endpoint or share the sample export template by Friday 7/23
- Align on the final rubric cells in the sheet (I attached a first draft)

Attachments: poc-success-criteria-templates.xlsx, eval-rubric-v1.md

If you'd like, Stephanie can run through the rubric and proposed acceptance gates on a 30-min call — happy to set that up.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the clear write-up — that matches our notes. A few quick clarifications from our side: 
- Live traffic access: we can provide a redacted stream from our messaging queue but only for 1 week and only if we can do pre-filtering on PII.
- Offline export: we have ~1,800 labeled tickets that map to your extraction fields; happy to run that through an offline harness if you recommend it.

For risk reasons we were leaning toward the offline batch initially, but after reading your pros/cons I think shadow would give us the best signal for latency risk. Can we do a hybrid: run a short 3–4 day shadow window on a small subset (about 10% traffic) plus an offline run on the labeled set to validate extraction metrics?

If that works, we need:
1) A template for the export schema (send by 7/23)
2) A short onboarding doc for the shadow endpoint (network IPs, auth, expected throughput)

Let's pencil a 30-min session next week to align. I'm available Mon 7/26 in the morning PST.

Appreciate it — Alex
